title: Secret Anagram
statement:
Two words are **anagrams** if you can rearrange the letters of the first word to get the second one. For example `listen` and `silent` are anagrams: they use exactly the same letters the same number of times.

Given two words, check whether they are anagrams of each other.
input: The first line contains the word **a**. The second line contains the word **b**. Both words consist of lowercase English letters.
output: Print `YES` if the words are anagrams and `NO` otherwise.
constraints: 1 ≤ length of a, length of b ≤ 10^5

samples.explanation: `apple` has two letters p and no r, `paper` has two letters p and one r.

hints: If the lengths differ, the answer is immediately `NO`.
Count how many times each of the 26 letters appears in each word and compare the counts. Sorting both words also works.
editorial:
Make an array `cnt` of 26 zeros. Add 1 for every letter of a and subtract 1 for every letter of b. The words are anagrams exactly when all 26 counters end at zero. Alternatively, sort both words and compare them (O(n log n)).

Complexity: O(n + 26).
